notes:
Summary: Skyward is an enterprise fintech building a customer-facing chat assistant and real-time transaction reranking. They are serious about reserved capacity (dedicated) to meet latency SLOs and predictable unit economics.

Workload profile (from traces):
- Baseline steady-state: ~120 QPS (concurrent sessions steady traffic).
- Average tokens per request: 300 tokens. At 120 QPS -> ~36k tokens/sec sustained.
- Peak bursts: up to 380–420 QPS for ~5–15 minutes (campaigns and batch retries).
- Token/sec burst estimate: ~120k tokens/sec at peak.

Targets and constraints:
- Latency SLOs requested: p95 <= 200ms (chat generation), p99 <= 450ms (critical fraud flows).
- Throughput guarantee: sustained 36k tokens/sec with 3x burst headroom during business hours.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; prefer quantized model variants where acceptable.
- Deployment: customer requires VPC private networking, KMS integration, SOC2 compliance, and EU data residency for some customers.

Recommended workshop outcomes (2-day):
Day 1: trace ingestion, token distribution validation, map hot paths (reranking vs generation), identify caching opportunities (prefix caching on common prompts).
Day 2: synthetic load replay (steady + burst profiles), latency tail analysis, draft reserved GPU plan and fallback model matrix.

Initial sizing recommendation (workshop to validate):
- Serving mix: 70% Llama2-13B 8-bit quantized for conversational flows, 30% 70B-class for high-fidelity fraud explainability routes.
- Estimated reserved GPUs: 10–14 x H100-equivalent (or 16–20 x A100-80GB equiv) to meet sustained 36k tokens/sec with 3x burst headroom and p99 targets. Final number depends on batching and KV-cache efficiency.
- Autoscale/burst plan: Keep dedicated reserved pool sized for steady-state + modest burst; enable overflow to a burst pool (lower-priority or cheaper instances) with clear fallback model that preserves correctness for critical flows.

SLA negotiation notes:
- Skyward expects contractual p95 and p99 latency SLOs for dedicated capacity. They are open to tiered pricing for tighter SLOs and higher dedicated minimums.
- Must include uptime SLA, maintenance windows, and clear fallback behavior when capacity exceeded.
- Legal wants explicit language around data residency, KMS handling, and audit log retention.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- CTO (paraphrase): "We cannot compromise on p99 for fraud detection flows; cost can be optimized by using quantized models for chat."
- Head of Infra: "Need a predictable reserved GPU plan — monthly billing with clear burst policy."

Next actions (short):
- AE to confirm dates for 2-day onsite (target week of 2026-03-22).
- SE to prepare synthetic load scripts (shape: steady 120 QPS, 15-min bursts to 420 QPS, token distribution from traces).
- Send updated SLA template with data residency & KMS clauses to legal (drive:/Skyward/Security_QA_Sheet.docx).

Risk/Blockers: pending legal sign-off on residency, network egress caps with their cloud provider, final GPU budget approval by CFO.
